subject: plotting something visually like stat_smooth, but with set range

messages.author: b3134ba1532e6a34
messages.subject: plotting something visually like stat_smooth, but with set range
parts:
I have the following data:
Std_Curve Accept_Error(%) Est_QC
5 20% 5.5
20 20% 25
50 15% 40
100 15% 130
500 10% 700
1000 10% 1500


I am trying to set-up a plot that emulates the look of a stat_smooth, with a unity line running through the Std_Curve, then a shaded background representing the acceptable error around the Std_Curve (based on the Accept_Error %), and then overplot the points of the estimated quality control samples to see if my assay conditions are impacting the QC samples in a systematic way.   Any help would be greatly appreciated.  

Thanks -
Matthew

--
R. Matthew Strother, MD

Medical Oncology

messages.author: 20c6dbb46920d12c
messages.subject: Re: plotting something visually like stat_smooth, but with set range
parts:
Hi,

I think geom_ribbon is what you need to manually depict the error range. Does this do it?

ggplot(dr_data, aes(1:6,Std_Curve)) +

geom_smooth() +

geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=Std_Curve-Std_Curve*Accept_Error,ymax=Std_Curve+Std_Curve*Accept_Error),alpha=.2) +

geom_point(aes(x,Est_QC))




Adam Loveland
